scope: Dispatch UI section events, independent GPS and daily counters

behavior.bootstrap: One authorized jobs/roster/config/signals request; explicit protocol capability is required and no heavier admin/driver fallback remains.
behavior.changes: Section versions coalesce into one request for only changed visible groups. Responses acknowledge selected pre-hydration versions; newer events stay pending.
behavior.locations: Exact displayed active-job subscriptions check assignment bindings. GPS changes patch coordinates without business calls. Terminal/assignment access loss clears the point and reconciles jobs once per failed binding.
behavior.dailyCounters: One current Vietnam-day aggregate subscription. Midnight switches that document only; yesterday counts disappear locally even while recovery is paused.
behavior.visibility: Hidden/offline detaches all subscriptions. Settings retains only current-account and configuration subscriptions. Unchanged resume makes no business request.
behavior.access: Account-keyed UI and current-profile listener clear private data on revocation. Late account/authority responses and mutations are fenced. Mutation recovery requires a successful authorized snapshot.
behavior.drafts: Unedited configuration follows updates; changed drafts and their expected revision survive background reads. Assignment refreshes jobs/roster only; saving configuration refreshes config only.
behavior.scopeLabels: Show whole-scope active-job total and explicitly disclose capped job/roster display; page-only empty states do not imply a complete empty queue.

validation.notes: The base browser suite passed 67 cases; the wrapper command then reported no matching tests in its unrelated history suite because --grep was forwarded to that second command. This is not recorded as a complete npm test:data-cost-ui pass. The initial 108-case delivery run had a mobile long clock-advance test failure; the final deterministic midnight and all dispatch cases passed.

release.backendPrerequisite: PR26: selective callable, all section source triggers and named Firestore rules serving and verified, after PR24/25.
release.rollback: Revert this frontend to PR25 to restore the legacy full dispatch reader. PR26 continues accepting legacy requests. Do not independently roll back the separate location writer/readers from PR24.

remaining: The roster cap and bounded delivery page require a separate cursor UI.
Per-driver count queries still occur on roster changes; GPS/rules/listener reconnects have costs.
Mutation/source acknowledgements can still require a later reconciliation when a source trigger arrives after the immediate read.
Actual Enterprise units, request latency and currency savings require post-release observation.
